svg.title: Bench breadboard layout, drawn to a real 400-point half-size board
svg.desc: Three 400-point half-size breadboards, 30 columns by 10 rows plus four power rails. Board A carries the Teensy 4.1 straddling the centre channel, with rail-bridge jumpers taking its 3V3 supply to the upper rails, 10k pull-ups and 1nF on the quadrature columns and 4.7k on the I2C columns. Board B carries the two Hall latches, board C the AS5600.
svg.text: Bench layout — drawn to a real 400-point half-size board
30 columns × 10 rows + four rails = 400 tie points, which is the SZH-BBAD-005 that was ordered. A pale band = one node. A gap = passes over, not into.
BOARD B — DRIVE: two Hall latches, BOTH ON THE SAME HUB
Only one rear wheel is instrumented. The pair sits 6.80 mm apart on that one carrier — a quarter cycle out of step, which is what
gives direction. One latch counts; it cannot tell forward from reverse. A and B are two sensors on one wheel, not one sensor on each of two.
from the E-stop COIL node — the NC side
10 kΩ from the coil node, 2.7 kΩ
on to GND. The junction is the pin.
High while the authority chain is
blown coil fuse, dead logic pack
METER IT before it touches the pin.
the pins land UNDER the body — you connect in the rows above and below
The AS5600 breakout may carry its own pull-ups. If it does, the 4.7 kΩ on board A are in parallel — fine.
Rows A–E of every board are left unused here. That is normal; a half-size board has far more holes than this needs.
